Detroit Casinos Report $110.5M in October Revenue as MotorCity Outgrows Its Rivals

Published November 12, 2026 · 3 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Detroit's three commercial casinos reported a combined $110.5 million in October 2026 revenue, the Michigan Gaming Control Board said November 10, with table games and slots accounting for $108.1 million and retail sports betting contributing $2.4 million in qualified adjusted gross receipts.

A mixed month across the three properties

Table-games-and-slots revenue rose 2.1% year over year and 5.2% from September, but the growth wasn't evenly spread across Detroit's casinos. MotorCity Casino posted $35.2 million, up 15.6% from October 2025, the strongest performance of the three. MGM Grand Detroit brought in $51.3 million, down 2.7% year over year, while Hollywood Casino at Greektown reported $21.6 million, down 5.0%. That gave MGM a 47% market share for the month, with MotorCity at 33% and Hollywood Casino at Greektown at 20%.

Year to date through October, table-games-and-slots revenue across the three casinos is up 2.3% compared with the same period in 2025.

Sports betting and tax figures

Retail sports betting handle for the month totaled $12.87 million, with qualified adjusted gross receipts of $2.4 million — up 56.0% from October 2025 and up $1.6 million from September. MGM's retail sportsbook generated $746,215 in receipts, MotorCity's $928,607, and Hollywood Casino at Greektown's $729,350.

The three casinos paid $8.8 million in state gaming taxes for October, compared with $8.6 million a year earlier, and submitted $13.4 million in wagering taxes and development-agreement payments to the City of Detroit. Retail sports betting separately generated $90,878 in state taxes and $111,073 in wagering taxes to the city.

Why it matters

Detroit's monthly casino revenue reports are a closely watched indicator of commercial gaming health in Michigan, and October's numbers show a market where overall growth is real but uneven — MotorCity's double-digit gain more than offset mid-single-digit declines at its two competitors. The retail sportsbook growth, while a small share of total revenue, continues a pattern of year-over-year gains that has held for most of 2026.
